rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results - two-year field experiment (2015-2016) at Sichuan Agricultural University farm comparing soybean growth, leaf anatomy, photosynthesis and yield under two maize-soybean relay-strip intercropping row configurations (A1, A2) and sole soybean (CK).
rows.notes: The study contains no drip irrigation (or any irrigation treatment) and no root measurements; it reports effects of maize shading and subsequent light recovery on soybean morphology, leaf anatomy, chlorophyll, photosynthetic rate and per-plant yield. It does not report a 34% increase in corn root development or any comparison of drip fertigation with traditional irrigation methods. The claim appears to be a misattribution; the cited study is on intercropping light environment, not on drip irrigation.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a primary field experiment on shading in maize-soybean relay-strip intercropping; it has no irrigation technology component whatsoever, so it cannot support the drip/crop_production claim.
